question: When a spinner's turn starts over right on a ruler number, where should the restart label go and what should it say?
context: The spinner mock (icon-loop-wt, step 5) labels the restart "and again" under the lanes; the bell and knob mocks label it "repeats" up on the ruler. A lone 800 ms spinner restarts exactly on the ruler's 800, where the two labels used to print over each other.

options.label: "repeats", just under the 800
options.summary: The blue dashed line keeps the word every loop page uses, and when it would sit on a ruler number it drops one line, so it reads just under the 800 beside the line. The strip stays the same height.
pros: Same word as the bell and knob pages
Built and shown in the audit picture
cons: Not where the spinner mock draws it (below the last lane)
options.mitigation: Between ruler numbers it stays up on the ruler, exactly as the bell page draws it.

options.label: "and again", below the last lane
options.summary: Do what the spinner mock shows: the label reads "and again" and sits under the last lane, below the bars. The strip grows a short row under the lanes to hold it.
pros: Matches the spinner page word for word
cons: The strip gets taller only for some loops
Two words for one mark across the loop pages
options.mitigation: The extra row could be there for every loop, so the height never jumps.

options.label: "repeats", below the last lane
options.summary: Keep the word "repeats" but put it under the last lane whenever it would land on a ruler number, the way the spinner mock places its label.
pros: Placement as the spinner mock draws it
cons: The strip grows a short row under the lanes
options.mitigation: Same as b: a row held for every loop.

answer.note: Taken as recommended: the user, 2026-10-19, said there were too many cards, most did not matter and they could not follow them. Change it later only if they complain about the result
